fix_decisions.claim_text: Criterion 34 requires a request that runs today with no rule-set file to run with the same result; iteration two's key-limit tightening also reached that path, so a request carrying 64 extras beside the declared progressToken now had its metadata discarded.
fix_decisions.evidence: Read src/sqllens/server.py lines 195-260 and confirmed the defect: the tightened count was unconditional, so it changed behaviour criterion 34 requires to stay unchanged. The iteration-two disclosure did not settle it, because criterion 34's case is a result the criterion requires to be identical, not a limit the fix may tighten. Fixed by scoping the departure to the case criterion 10 actually decides: _request_metadata takes count_declared_keys, counts every key the caller sent only under it, and the query_database tool passes cfg.rule_sets.loaded is not None, so criterion 10's refusal holds under a rule-set file while criterion 34's no-rule-set behaviour returns to what it was. Both bounds remain, so neither path fails open. Acceptance-criteria comparison: criterion 10 ('A request whose _meta has more than 64 keys is refused as rule-set key missing') decides the 65-key rule-set case, where the flag is on and the request is still refused as rule-set key missing; criterion 34 ('With no rule-set file configured, a query_database request that runs today runs with the same result ...') decides the no-rule-set case, where the count is again the extras alone, so the result matches the base commit; criterion 8's five request classes are unchanged. The PR body's Stricter than criterion disclosure was removed, because the departure it disclosed no longer exists and leaving it would be a false claim. Binding instructions: nothing in AGENTS.md or the loaded extensions forbids the fix; the sqlglot rule does not apply. Class sweep: _request_metadata has one production call site, confirmed by git grep. Verification: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q, 3192 passed; .venv/bin/ruff check ., all checks passed. New tests pin both arms of the flag and the call-site wiring.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The rule-set key-limit test hard-coded the flag and used a fixture with 65 extras, so it would pass with the flag off too and pinned neither the declared-key branch nor the new call-site wiring.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct. Fixed by moving the fixture to exactly 64 extras beside the declared progressToken, so only the declared-key count refuses it, and by asserting on the same context that the request is forwarded whole with the flag off. Added test_query_database_counts_declared_meta_keys_only_under_rule_sets, which builds the server for a rule-set config and a plain config and asserts the flag the tool passes is [True, False], so hard-coding it either way fails.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The transcribed query_database excerpt still showed the old _request_metadata(ctx) call shape after the delta changed it.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct. The excerpt now shows the call with count_declared_keys, matching the code.

phase3_findings.description: docs/external/rule-sets.md line 99 says serve and validate both print a warning for an unconfirmed set; serve emits it through the sqllens.rule_sets logger before logging is configured.

docs/external/rule-sets.md line 125 claims the decimal-string equivalence holds everywhere, which is false of the file itself, and line 145 tells the operator to restart although the same sentence says the check retries on the next request.

The runner call orders in docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md lines 185 and 191, docs/internal/agent/factory.md line 87 and docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md line 209 omit the two new runners.
The AGENTS.md architecture tree gains no entry for src/sqllens/rule_sets.py or src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py.
src/sqllens/cli.py line 167 separates _unconfirmed_rule_sets from the preceding definition with one blank line instead of two.

src/sqllens/cli.py lines 99-119: _rule_set_file_configured swallows OSError, UnicodeDecodeError and TOMLDecodeError and answers False with no log record, so the operator never learns that verify-memory does not support rule sets in the case the branch exists for.

src/sqllens/server.py lines 243-252 discard the whole of _meta at debug level when a future SDK stops exposing model_fields_set; with a rule-set file every request would then be refused with nothing above debug to explain it, unlike the sibling branch, which warns.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py lines 234-358 keep several invariants at call sites rather than in the types: the indexed-file docstring, the public mutable confirmed latch that preflight writes without the lock, the unbounded rule_sets list, and the unconstrained RuleSetSelection.
src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py lines 470-472 rebuild the refusal behind its own constructor, so a future stateful subclass would be re-raised half-built.
src/sqllens/agent/factory.py lines 91-105: the rule-set user resolver falls back to the shared built-in user with no log record when no selection is published.

src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py lines 61-64 and docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md line 57 state both prompt rules unconditionally, without the dialect and base-prompt conditions that decide them.
tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py line 8 describes the example set as listing a predicate column the shared example lacks.
docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md line 3 records a freshness marker five commits behind the branch head.
docs/external/configuration.md line 234 still frames row-rule blocks as unlike other sections in rejecting unknown keys.
No test covers that list_data_sources answers a call carrying no request metadata while a rule-set file is configured, nor that the bundle manifest gains no rule-set entry.
